3.1.1.notes: No Cartesia primary source retrieved this session states the TLS version used for data in transit. The DPA Annex II (www.cartesia.ai/legal/dpa) requires measures so data 'cannot be read, copied, modified or deleted without authorization during electronic transmission', but names no standard. A third-party site claimed 'TLS 1.3' — disallowed as a source, not used. Searched: www.cartesia.ai/legal/dpa, trust.cartesia.ai (unfetchable), docs.cartesia.ai, cartesia.ai/blog/gdpr-compliance. NOTE FOR FILLER: the 3.1.1 dropdown has no 'Not known' option — leave blank or use 'Others - pls indicate below' pending the vendor's written answer; do not guess a TLS version.

3.1.2.notes: No Cartesia primary source retrieved this session names an encryption-at-rest standard (AES-128/192/256 etc.). A third-party site claimed 'AES-256 at rest' — disallowed as a source, not used. Searched: www.cartesia.ai/legal/dpa (Annex II excerpts retrieved mention encryption only for 'archived data media', no algorithm), trust.cartesia.ai (403 on every fetch attempt — likely documents this), docs.cartesia.ai, privacy policy. 'Not known' is a valid dropdown option for this row.

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented with a standard. The DPA Annex II (www.cartesia.ai/legal/dpa) does list 'encryption of archived data media' among its technical and organizational measures — so archived/backup media are stated to be encrypted — but no algorithm is named, and per form_spec the dropdown wants a standard. 'Not known' with this note is the honest answer; ask the vendor which algorithm covers backups.

3.1.4.notes: No Cartesia primary source retrieved this session describes key management or who generates encryption keys (no CMEK/BYOK documentation found on docs.cartesia.ai excerpts). The playbook default for managed cloud ('Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)') is plausible but would be an industry-norm inference, which the hard rules forbid. Ask the vendor; also confirm with the human whether Tavus has any customer-managed-key arrangement with Cartesia.

3.1.6.notes: No Cartesia primary source retrieved this session states whether Cartesia can anonymize customer personal data. Cartesia offers 'optional Zero Data Retention' (vendor pages, e.g. GDPR blog / docs onboarding flow) — that is deletion/non-retention, not anonymization, so it does not answer this row. Searched DPA, privacy policy, docs.cartesia.ai, trust center (unfetchable).

3.1.7.notes: No Cartesia primary source retrieved this session states a pseudonymization capability. The DPA references the EU SCCs (which nominally require pseudonymization/encryption 'as appropriate' in Annex II), but no retrieved excerpt shows Cartesia asserting it pseudonymizes customer personal data. Ask the vendor.
